reuse.why: Builds on the existing recurConfigToRSchedule, applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay and getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and the new range handler reuses them and the getUpcomingDates pattern rather than re-deriving recurrence logic.

duplication.why: Every RSchedule construction now has to pair recurConfigToRSchedule(config) with getHolidayExdates(config) by hand (four sites), and getDatesInRange restates the daily-vs-other weekend decision with its own frequency check.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday rules live in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing weekend helpers, the handler lives in schedules/app.ts with the other handlers; the 100-year MM-DD expansion into exdates is an awkward fit for the recurrence layer.

scope.why: Edits are confined to schedule date logic, its callers, the new handler, the type, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The daily-skip rule is split across byDayOfWeek in recurConfigToRSchedule, holiday exdates expanded for 100 years, and a frequency check in getDatesInRange, so a maintainer must keep several mechanisms consistent and remember to add exdates at every new RSchedule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange (schedules/app.ts) decides itself whether to apply applyWeekendRule via `config.frequency !== 'daily'` instead of the shared weekend rule deciding it, unlike getNextDate/getUpcomingDates.

disguised_duplication.where: The 'daily schedules skip, others move' rule appears as byDayOfWeek in recurConfigToRSchedule, as the frequency guard in getHolidayExdates, and again as moveWeekend in getDatesInRange; the rrules+exdates pairing is repeated at app.ts (x2), find-schedules.ts and rule-utils.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: holidays parameter added to applyWeekendRule, applyWeekendRuleToDay and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; daily/skipWeekend branch added in recurConfigToRSchedule, daily-only guard and MM-DD branch in getHolidayExdates; getDatesInRange wraps applyWeekendRule in its own frequency condition.
